chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Pre-emption (shuf'ah) does not occur except for two partners as long as they have not divided (the property). So when they become three, there is no pre-emption for one of them.

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption, the right of a co-owner to buy out another's share before it is sold to an outsider.
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةً: Three, indicating the number of partners after which the rule changes.
key_terms.لِشَرِيكَيْنِ: For two partners, indicating the specific condition of partnership number.
key_terms.يُقَاسِمَا: They divide/share, referring to the partition of the co-owned property.

ai.seo_question: When does the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) cease in co-owned property according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the scope of pre-emption (shuf'ah) by limiting it to a binary partnership, reflecting the Shia juristic view that complexity in ownership dilutes the individual right to preempt. It highlights the legal principle that as the number of co-owners increases beyond two, the potential for conflicting claims makes the right of pre-emption impractical for any single partner. This ruling underscores the importance of clear property division and the prevention of disputes in communal ownership structures.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said :
‘The pre-emption does not take place except for the two partners for as long as their share has not bee distributed. So when they become three, so there is no pre-emption for one of them’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn ‘Abd af- Rahman from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Al-Shuf’ (one’s rights of pre-emption) is applicable only between two partners who have not concluded the partnership. If they become three then one of them does not have such right.’”
